## Summary

Implemented SPEC.md §5 (Transcribe / Speech):

- **`ios/SparklingGo/SparklingGo/MethodServices/SpeechModule.swift`** (new) — a `LynxModule` wrapping `SFSpeechRecognizer`: `getAuthorizationStatus`, `requestAuthorization`, and `transcribeSample`, which loads the bundled `sample.wav` via `SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` with `shouldReportPartialResults = true` and invokes the JS callback repeatedly (`partial`/`final`/`error` events).
- **`RouterServiceImpl.swift`** — registered `SpeechModule` alongside `HealthKitModule` in the router's `lynxModule` dict so it's available on the Transcribe page.
- **`project.pbxproj`** — added `INFOPLIST_KEY_NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` to both Debug/Release configs (Speech needs no entitlement, just this usage string).
- **`public/sample.wav`** (new) — feeds `spec-assets/sample.wav` through rsbuild's public-dir convention so `npm run build` reliably bundles it into `dist/` → iOS `Resources/Assets/` on every build, rather than depending on a file that was already sitting there outside the build pipeline.
- **`src/typing.d.ts`** — typed the `SpeechModule` native interface.
- **`src/pages/transcribe/App.vue`** — wired the full screen: status line reflecting auth state (refreshed on show), `Request Access`, `Transcribe Sample` (enabled only when granted and not running), live-streaming partial transcript, final transcript with `Completed in N.N s` (wall-clock via `Date.now()`), and error text surfaced in the status line on failure.

**Verified:** `npm run build && xcodebuild ...` succeeds. Installed and launched on the iOS Simulator via `idb`/`simctl`: navigated Home → Transcribe, requested access (the custom usage-description text appeared correctly in the system dialog), granted access, and status/button states updated exactly per spec. Confirmed persistence of the process (no crash) throughout, including when tapping "Transcribe Sample."

One caveat worth flagging: on this sandbox's simulator, `SFSpeechRecognizer` reports zero supported locales (verified independently — the same API works fine on the host Mac directly, 63 locales), so the actual transcription never starts here; the app correctly surfaces this as "Failed to initialize recognizer" in the status line rather than crashing, satisfying the spec's error-handling requirement. This looks like a simulator/environment asset-provisioning limitation rather than an app bug, but it means the live transcription (word-overlap accuracy check in §6) hasn't been exercised end-to-end here — worth confirming on a real device or a simulator with speech assets available.
